title: Proper surjective base change is coherent and conservative on vanishing topoi
statement: Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], let $f:X\to S$ be of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let $p:T\to S$ be proper and surjective [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism]. Form $X_T=X\times_S T$, $f_T:X_T\to T$, and the induced geometric morphism $v:V_{f_T}\to V_f$ of [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles]. The scheme $T$ is Noetherian and $f_T$ is of finite presentation. Both $V_f$ and $V_{f_T}$ are coherent topoi, and $v$ is coherent and conservative, in the terminology of [def-trf-coherent-topos].

source.place: Author draft, §8.1, printed p. 17 (coherence of the triple sites), and proof of Lemma 9.1.5, printed p. 21 (lifting points and coherence of the induced base-change morphism); Noetherian finite-presentation specialization. The preliminary scheme assertions are Stacks 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian) and 01TS (lemma-base-change-finite-presentation). Read online; local archival copy WANTED in report.md.

proof.text: Properness of $p$ includes finite type. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] gives that $T$ is Noetherian. Finite presentation of $f$ implies finite type: in an affine presentation, a finitely presented algebra is finitely generated. Thus the same lemma gives that $X$ is Noetherian. By clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], $f_T$ is of finite presentation, and consequently of finite type, so $X_T$ is Noetherian as well. Each of $S,T,X,X_T$ is quasi-compact by the definition of Noetherian and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. The morphisms $f,f_T$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated by finite presentation.

source.place: Tags 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian), 01TS (lemma-base-change-finite-presentation); quasi-separatedness of locally Noetherian schemes is Properties Tag 01OY.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-qcqs-oriented-triple-presentation] to the diagrams $X\to S\leftarrow S$ and $X_T\to T\leftarrow T$; the right-hand arrows are identities. Step 1 verifies every quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness hypothesis. These give small sites $\mathcal C,\mathcal C_T$ with finite limits for $V_f,V_{f_T}$, whose topologies are generated by finite families of types (a), (b) and singleton families of type (c). Since these generating families are finite and the categories have fibre products, the pretopology they generate (finite composites of base changes of such families) again consists of finite families, so the topologies are generated by finite-cover pretopologies; this is the description of the pretopology in the proof of Exposé XI, Lemma 2.5. By [lem-trf-finitary-site-coherent-generators], the associated representables $H_Z$ and $H_{Z_T}$ are coherent generators. The criterion also supplies a generating subcategory of coherent objects closed under finite limits; therefore both topoi are coherent.

source.place: Exposé XI, proof of Lemma 2.5; Orgogozo §8.1, printed p. 17, triple-site coherence.

proof.text:
For $Z=(U\to V\leftarrow W)$ in $\mathcal C$, the presentation lemma identifies
$$v^{-1}H_Z\simeq H_{Z_T},\qquad Z_T=(U\times_X X_T\to V\times_S T\leftarrow W\times_S T).$$
The three components are separated etale of finite presentation over $X_T,T,T$, respectively, so $Z_T$ belongs to $\mathcal C_T$. Step 2 makes its associated representable coherent. Thus $v^{-1}$ takes every member of the chosen coherent generating family to a coherent object. Apply the morphism criterion in [lem-trf-finitary-site-coherent-generators]: it gives preservation of all coherent objects, which is precisely coherence of $v$. This assertion uses no surjectivity hypothesis.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 9.1.5, printed p. 21, coherence seen on the sites; inverse-image formula is Exposé XI 1.6 and functoriality 1.9.

proof.text: The finite-cover site $\mathcal C$ has enough points by [lem-trf-finitary-site-enough-points]. Every point $z$ of $V_f$ is described by its two projection points and structural $2$-morphism, by [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal]. By [lem-trf-etale-topos-points-geometric], those projection points can be represented by geometric points $\bar x$ of $X$ and $\bar t$ of $S$. Conjugating the structural arrow by their point isomorphisms identifies $z$ with the triple $(\bar x,\bar t,c)$, where $c:\bar t\Rightarrow f(\bar x)$. The universal property's uniqueness clause identifies the points themselves, including the arrow $c$, rather than merely their projections.

source.place: Exposé XI 1.8, point triples; Stacks 00YQ (proposition-criterion-points) and 04HU (lemma-points-small-etale-site).

proof.text: Fix a triple $(\bar x,\bar t,c)$ from step 4 and write $\bar s=f\bar x$, represented on the same algebraically closed field $\Omega_s$ as $\bar x$. Apply [lem-trf-proper-geometric-specialization-lift] to $p$ and this prescribed $c:\bar t\Rightarrow\bar s$. It supplies extensions $r_s,r_t$, geometric points $\bar s',\bar t'$ of $T$, and $c':\bar t'\Rightarrow\bar s'$ with $p\bar s'=\bar s r_s$, $p\bar t'=\bar t r_t$, carrying $c'$ to precisely $c$ under the extension isomorphisms. Properness is what permits lifting the specialization to its special endpoint; surjectivity permits the initial lift over its general endpoint. We do not prescribe an arbitrary special lift in $T$.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 9.1.5, printed p. 21: lifting points; the geometric-specialization input is isolated in its own scheme lemma.

proof.text: The scheme maps $\bar x r_s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega'_s\to X$ and $\bar s':\operatorname{Spec}\Omega'_s\to T$ agree after composition to $S$. The fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] therefore gives a geometric point $\bar x_T$ of $X_T$ with projections $\bar x r_s$ and $\bar s'$. In particular $f_T\bar x_T=\bar s'$, so $(\bar x_T,\bar t',c')$ gives a point $z_T$ of $V_{f_T}$ by [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal]. By [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-morphism-stalk-bijection], the images $\bar x r_s$ and $\bar t r_t$ have canonically the same etale point functors as $\bar x$ and $\bar t$. The compatibility $pc'=c$ from step 5 identifies the structural arrows as well. Uniqueness in the oriented-product universal property now gives an isomorphism $vz_T\simeq z$. Thus every point of $V_f$ lifts up to isomorphism, as required for stalk testing.

source.place: Exposé XI 1.4, 1.8–1.9; Stacks 04FN (remark-map-stalks) for the field-extension isomorphisms.

proof.text:
Let $a:F\to G$ be a morphism of sheaves of sets on $V_f$ for which $v^{-1}a$ is invertible. For each point $z$ in the conservative family of step 4, choose $z_T$ and $vz_T\simeq z$ as in step 6. Functorial composition of inverse images gives
$$z^{-1}a\simeq z_T^{-1}v^{-1}a,$$
which is invertible. The enough-points criterion [lem-trf-finitary-site-enough-points] implies that $a$ is invertible. Hence $v^{-1}$ reflects isomorphisms, exactly the definition of conservativity in [def-trf-coherent-topos]. This proves conservativity on set sheaves without changing coefficient categories. Together with steps 1–3, it proves all the assertions.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 9.1.5, printed p. 21: surjectivity on points implies conservativity; Stacks 00YQ (proposition-criterion-points).
